outcome_detail: Federal lawsuit filed in early September 2025 (reported September 4, 2025) against the Town of Killen, Police Chief Bryan Hammond, and former officer Jarrod Webster, seeking damages for constitutional violations, permanent injuries, mental anguish, and lost wages. Newly pending as of the most recent coverage; no resolution reported as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: Webster was arrested on a rape charge in November 2023 following a misconduct investigation. He pleaded guilty on March 4, 2025 to one federal count of deprivation of rights under color of law (for the November 12, 2023 traffic-stop sexual assault) and one count of sexual exploitation of children (soliciting sexually explicit images from a minor between 2016 and 2018), and was sentenced in 2025 to 180 months (15 years) in federal prison.
description: A Meridianville woman, identified as Jane Doe, filed a federal lawsuit in September 2025 against the Town of Killen, Alabama, Police Chief Bryan Hammond, and former Killen police officer Jarrod Webster over a November 12, 2023 traffic stop. According to the complaint, Webster ordered her out of her vehicle, handcuffed and falsely imprisoned her, and threatened her with criminal charges and further detention unless she engaged in sexual acts with him. Webster pleaded guilty in March 2025 to a federal civil rights violation for sexually assaulting the woman during the stop, as well as to sexual exploitation of a child, and was sentenced to 15 years in federal prison. The suit alleges that Chief Hammond and the town failed to train Webster regarding sexual misconduct and were aware of what it describes as his regular and methodical abuse of his role to falsely imprison and sexually abuse women. The plaintiff seeks damages for constitutional violations, permanent injuries, mental anguish, and lost wages.
